schemes.title: Gopabandhu Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY GJAY Card)
schemes.department: Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Odisha (State Health Assurance Society), with the National Health Authority
schemes.brief: Odisha's free hospital cover, run together with Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY since April 2025. It replaced the old Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana (BSKY) card. Each family with an NFSA or state food security ration card gets cashless treatment of up to Rs 5 lakh a year at empanelled private and government hospitals in Odisha and outside, and women in the family get Rs 5 lakh more once the family limit is used up. Treatment in Odisha government hospitals is free for everyone, with or without a card. The card is the co-branded Ayushman (PMJAY-GJAY) card, which you can make yourself on the Ayushman portal or free at a CSC or a hospital's Ayushman desk.
schemes.benefit: Rs 5 lakh a year per family, plus Rs 5 lakh more for women members (up to Rs 10 lakh), cashless
eligibility: Families holding an NFSA or State Food Security Scheme (SFSS) ration card in Odisha
Families on the central PM-JAY list (SECC 2011), and families who already hold a PMJAY-GJAY card
Every person aged 70 and above, whatever the income, under the Ayushman Vay Vandana card
Women members get an extra Rs 5 lakh after the family's Rs 5 lakh for the year is used up
Anyone, card or no card, gets free medicines, tests, dialysis, chemotherapy, ICU and admission in Odisha government hospitals, from sub-centre to medical college
No limit on family size or age; illnesses you already have are covered
documents: Aadhaar card of each family member, for e-KYC
NFSA or SFSS ration card of the family
Mobile number for the OTP
A live photo, taken on the phone or at the centre during e-KYC
At the hospital: the PMJAY-GJAY card, with photocopies of the ration card and Aadhaar card

demoFields.label: Login as
demoFields.hint: Choose Beneficiary when you are making the card for yourself or your family, not Operator.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Any number you keep with you. The login OTP comes here, and so does the message when the card is approved.

demoFields.label: Scheme and state
demoFields.hint: Choose PMJAY and the state Odisha. In Odisha the same card is printed as the PMJAY-GJAY card.

demoFields.label: Search your family by
demoFields.hint: The ration card number brings up the whole family at once. If nothing comes, search again with your Aadhaar number.

demoFields.label: Ration card number
demoFields.hint: Copy the number from your NFSA or SFSS ration card exactly.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number for e-KYC
demoFields.hint: Aadhaar of the family member whose card you are making now. Each member is done one at a time.

demoFields.label: e-KYC method
demoFields.hint: Use Aadhaar OTP if the mobile is linked to Aadhaar, otherwise choose face authentication and scan the face with the phone camera.

demoFields.label: Live photo
demoFields.hint: Good light, face straight, no cap or dark glasses. A blurred photo gets the request sent back.

demoFields.label: Relation with head of family
demoFields.hint: How this member is related to the person named first on the ration card.

demoFields.label: District and PIN code
demoFields.hint: Where you live now, so the nearest empanelled hospitals are shown to you.

demoSteps: Open beneficiary.nha.gov.in (gjay.odisha.gov.in links to it under Know Your ABPMJAY GJAY Health Card Number) and log in as Beneficiary with your mobile number and OTP.
Choose PMJAY and Odisha, then search for your family by ration card number or Aadhaar. Members marked eKYC pending still need a card.
For each member, verify with Aadhaar OTP or face authentication, take the live photo and fill in mobile, relation, district and PIN code, then submit.

The state health agency checks the request and an SMS comes when it is approved. Log in again and download the card. If you have no smartphone, a CSC or the Ayushman desk of an empanelled hospital makes the card free.
At an empanelled hospital, go to the Ayushman Bharat counter with the card, ration card and Aadhaar. Your fingerprint or iris is checked at admission and again at discharge.
The hospital bills the government directly. Never pay cash for a treatment covered by the scheme. In Odisha government hospitals all treatment is free even without the card.
schemes.helpline: 104 (GJAY and state health helpline, toll-free) / 14555 (Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY helpline)

schemes.title: CM-KISAN Yojana (CM Kisan, earlier KALIA)
schemes.department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers' Empowerment, Government of Odisha (Directorate of Agriculture & Food Production)
schemes.brief: Odisha's own cash help for farmers, which replaced the KALIA scheme in September 2024. Small and marginal farmers get Rs 4,000 a year, Rs 2,000 before each crop season, on top of PM-KISAN's Rs 6,000, so most get Rs 10,000 a year in all. Landless farm-labour households in villages get Rs 12,500 in three instalments to start goat, poultry, duck, fishery, mushroom, bee or dairy work. One online registration on the CM KISAN portal covers both CM-KISAN and PM-KISAN, and from July 2026 an AgriStack Farmer ID is required.
schemes.benefit: Rs 4,000 a year (Rs 2,000 per crop season) for small and marginal farmers; Rs 12,500 in three instalments for landless households
eligibility: Small and marginal farmers, including sharecroppers who actually till the land, who are permanent residents of Odisha
Landless agricultural households in villages who live mainly on farm work, with an MGNREGA job card
Applicant must be 18 or older, and the family must hold a valid ration card. Only one member per family is paid; the family is worked out from the ration card
Land must be registered on Krushak Odisha, and an AgriStack Farmer ID is needed to register
Medium and large farmers get only PM-KISAN through the same portal, not CM-KISAN
Not for families with an income-tax payer, a government or PSU employee or pensioner, a present or former MP, MLA or minister, or a registered doctor, engineer, lawyer, CA or architect
documents: Aadhaar card, for OTP or fingerprint e-KYC
Ration card of the family
Bank passbook first page; the savings account must be linked to Aadhaar
Land record (RoR) registered on Krushak Odisha, for small and marginal farmers
AgriStack Farmer ID
MGNREGA job card, for landless agricultural households
A mobile number of your own that no other applicant has used

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Your own Aadhaar. A wrong or someone else's Aadhaar gets the application rejected. e-KYC is by OTP, or by fingerprint at a CSC or post office.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: A number in your own use that no other farmer has registered with. The OTP and payment messages come here.

demoFields.label: AgriStack Farmer ID
demoFields.hint: The farmer ID you got when your land was added to the Farmer Registry. Ask the Village Agriculture Worker if you do not have one.

demoFields.label: Applicant category
demoFields.hint: Choose Landless Agricultural Household (LAH) if you own no farm land but work on farms.

demoFields.label: Ration card number
demoFields.hint: Your family's ration card number. Only one person from a ration card can get CM-KISAN.

demoFields.label: District / Block / Gram Panchayat / Village
demoFields.hint: Where your family lives.

demoFields.label: Land details (from Krushak Odisha)
demoFields.hint: These come up from your Krushak Odisha record. Check that the khata and plot are really yours before going on.

demoFields.label: Bank account (Aadhaar-linked)
demoFields.hint: The money goes only to the account linked to your Aadhaar. Get it linked at your branch first.

demoFields.label: Upload documents
demoFields.value: Aadhaar, ration card, passbook page, RoR
demoFields.hint: Clear photos or scans. Landless households upload the MGNREGA job card instead of the RoR.

demoSteps: Before applying, register your land on Krushak Odisha and get your AgriStack Farmer ID (the Village Agriculture Worker or a CSC helps), and link Aadhaar to your bank account at the branch.
Open cmkisan.odisha.gov.in and click Farmer Registration. Read the instructions, tick the declaration, then verify your Aadhaar and mobile number with OTP.
Choose your category, fill in the ration card, address, land and bank details, upload the documents and submit. Note the token number shown.

The application is checked by the Village Agriculture Worker, the Block Agriculture Officer and the Chief District Agriculture Officer, and the Collector gives final approval. If a paper is wrong, the VAW sends it back for you to correct.
Track it under Check Status and e-KYC Status on the same portal, using the token number or Aadhaar.

Once approved, Rs 2,000 comes by DBT before the Kharif season (around Akshaya Tritiya) and Rs 2,000 before the Rabi season (around Nuakhai). PM-KISAN money comes separately from the same registration.
schemes.helpline: 155333 (Krushi Samrudhi Helpline, Agriculture Department) / 155261 or 1800-115-526 (PM-KISAN helpline)

schemes.title: MAMATA-PMMVY (Mamata Yojana)
schemes.department: Women & Child Development Department, Government of Odisha (with the Union Ministry of Women & Child Development for PMMVY)
schemes.brief: Cash help for a pregnant woman so she can eat well and rest before and after the birth. Since 1 April 2025 Odisha's old Mamata scheme and the central PMMVY run together as MAMATA-PMMVY, and the amount has gone up to Rs 10,000 for a boy and Rs 12,000 for a girl. It is paid in two instalments, for the first two live births (all births for PVTG families), straight into the mother's Aadhaar-linked account. You register at your Anganwadi Centre; the Anganwadi worker fills the form on the scheme's app, or you can self-register on the app.
schemes.benefit: Rs 10,000 for a boy, Rs 12,000 for a girl, in two instalments (first two live births)
eligibility: Pregnant women and new mothers living in Odisha, aged 18 years 7 months to 55 years on the date of the last period (LMP)

Must fit any one: SC or ST; 40% or more disability; ration card; Ayushman (PMJAY) card; e-Shram card; woman farmer getting PM-KISAN; MGNREGA job card; family income below Rs 8 lakh; or Anganwadi worker, helper or ASHA
Paid for the first two live births. Women of the 13 PVTG communities (Bonda, Juang, Dongria Kondh, Lanjia Saora and others) get it for every birth, until March 2029
Not for women whose own or husband's job is a regular Central or State government or PSU post, or whose family income is above Rs 8 lakh
First instalment: pregnancy registered at the Anganwadi and at least one check-up (ANC) within six months of the last period. Second: birth registered and all the baby's vaccines up to 14 weeks done
documents: Aadhaar card (compulsory)
Bank or post office account in her name only, linked to Aadhaar and DBT-enabled, with a photocopy of the passbook's first page
Mobile number linked to Aadhaar and the bank account
Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card, given free by the ANM when the pregnancy is registered
ABHA health ID number, made by the ANM
One proof of eligibility: caste certificate, disability certificate, Ayushman card, PM-KISAN, income certificate, ration card, e-Shram card, MGNREGA job card, or Anganwadi/ASHA identity card
For the second instalment: the baby's birth registration and vaccinations entered in the MCP card
schemes.submitAt: Your village or ward Anganwadi Centre. Go as soon as you know you are pregnant, within six months of your last period, and take your Aadhaar card, bank or post office passbook, mobile phone, MCP card, ABHA number and one eligibility proof (such as the ration card). The Anganwadi worker fills the form on the MAMATA-PMMVY app for you, free; you get an SMS on your phone as acknowledgement. For the second instalment, go back to the same Anganwadi Centre after the baby's 14-week vaccines.

demoFields.label: Name of beneficiary (as on Aadhaar)
demoFields.hint: The pregnant woman's own name, spelt exactly as on her Aadhaar card.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: The woman's own Aadhaar. Without it the form cannot be registered.

demoFields.label: Date of birth
demoFields.hint: She must be between 18 years 7 months and 55 years on the date of the last period.

demoFields.label: Husband's name
demoFields.hint: As written on the ration card or MCP card.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: A number linked to her Aadhaar and bank account. The acknowledgement and payment messages come here.

demoFields.label: Last menstrual period (LMP) date
demoFields.hint: The first day of the last period, as written in the MCP card. The first check-up must be within six months of this date.

demoFields.label: Number of living children
demoFields.hint: Count only children born alive and living. The scheme pays for the first two births (all births for PVTG families).

demoFields.label: MCP card number and ANC check-up date
demoFields.hint: From the MCP card the ANM gave you. If the check-up was done elsewhere, show the doctor's slip with the date.

demoFields.label: Proof of eligibility
demoFields.hint: Any one of the listed proofs is enough, for example the ration card, Ayushman card or job card.

demoFields.label: Bank account (Aadhaar-seeded)
demoFields.hint: A single-holder account in her own name, linked to Aadhaar. Money goes to the account linked last to her Aadhaar.

demoSteps: As soon as you know you are pregnant, register at the Anganwadi Centre, get the MCP card from the ANM, and have at least one check-up within six months of the last period.
Give the Anganwadi worker your Aadhaar, passbook, mobile number, MCP card, ABHA number and one eligibility proof. She registers you on the MAMATA-PMMVY app, and an SMS confirms the application.
After verification by the ICDS project office, the first instalment of Rs 6,000 comes by DBT into your Aadhaar-linked account.
Have the baby, get the birth registered at the health centre or Anganwadi, and complete all vaccines up to 14 weeks (at birth, 6, 10 and 14 weeks), all entered in the MCP card.
The Anganwadi worker sends the claim for the second instalment: Rs 4,000 more for a boy or Rs 6,000 more for a girl, again straight to your account.
Ask the Anganwadi worker for the status, or check it on the app. If money is late, tell the Anganwadi worker or the CDPO, or call 181.
schemes.helpline: 181 (Mamata and women's helpline, toll-free) / 1515 (PMMVY toll-free helpline)

schemes.title: Nirman Shramik Registration — OB&OCWW Board (Construction Worker Card)
schemes.department: Odisha Building & Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board, Labour & ESI Department, Government of Odisha
schemes.brief: Registers a construction worker with the Odisha welfare board and gives an identity card with a registration number. After one year on the register, the worker and family can claim the board's help: Rs 10,000 for each of two deliveries for women workers, Rs 50,000 for a daughter's or her own marriage, Rs 2,000 to Rs 40,000 a year for two children's studies, up to Rs 3 lakh for major illness, tools and bicycle money, and Rs 2 lakh (Rs 4 lakh if killed at work) to the family on death. Registration costs Rs 20 plus Rs 50 a year, and is done online on the NirmanShramik portal.
schemes.benefit: Worker card for board help — Rs 10,000 maternity, Rs 50,000 marriage, Rs 2,000–40,000 a year education, Rs 2–4 lakh death benefit
eligibility: Building or construction worker who has completed 18 years and not yet 60
At least 90 days of building or other construction work in the last 12 months
Not working in a factory or mine covered by the Factories Act or the Mines Act
Not a member of any other welfare fund, and not registered with another district or state's construction board
Workers from Odisha working in other states can also register
Pay Rs 50 every year to stay a member; missing three years in a row ends membership. Most benefits start after one year of registration
documents: Aadhaar card
Voter ID card (EPIC)
Certificate of 90 days' work from the employer, a registered trade union or the labour inspector, or a self-certificate giving sites, employers and days worked (model formats are on the portal)
Bank passbook first page showing the IFSC code
Proof of age
Recent passport-size colour photographs
Nominee details (Form XXXI): name, relation, age and share
Rs 20 registration fee, and Rs 50 yearly contribution
schemes.portalName: NirmanShramik — Odisha Building & Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board

demoFields.label: First name as per Aadhaar
demoFields.hint: Write it exactly as on your Aadhaar card.

demoFields.label: Surname as per Aadhaar
demoFields.hint: Your family name as on Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Sex

demoFields.label: Mobile number

demoFields.label: Are you a registered construction worker?
demoFields.hint: Choose No for a new registration. Choose Yes only if you already have a board registration number.

demoFields.label: Date of birth / age

demoFields.label: Permanent address (village, post office, GP, block, district)

demoFields.label: Establishments worked in last year, and days
demoFields.value: Maa Tarini Constructions, Jajpur Road — mason — 120 days
demoFields.hint: Each site or employer, the work you did and the days. The total must be at least 90.

demoFields.label: Bank account number / branch

demoSteps: Get your 90-day work certificate signed by your employer, a registered trade union or the labour inspector, or fill the self-certificate. Model formats are under Downloads on nirmanshramik.odisha.gov.in.
Open Construction Worker Login and click One Time Registration. Read the eligibility, tick the declaration, enter your name, sex and mobile number, and verify with OTP.

Log in with the OTP and fill the registration form: personal details, address, family, work done, bank account and nominee. Upload the photo, Aadhaar, voter ID, work certificate and passbook, then submit and note the application number.
The labour office (District or Assistant Labour Officer) checks the application. Pay the Rs 20 registration fee and the Rs 50 contribution when asked, and follow progress under Application Tracking.
Once approved you get a registration number and identity card. This is your construction worker card.
Pay Rs 50 every year under Pay Annual Contribution. After one year, apply from your login for maternity, marriage, education, tools, bicycle or medical help; the money comes to your bank account.
schemes.helpline: 155368 (Shramik Sahayata helpline, toll-free, 24x7, inside Odisha) / 1800-345-6703 (for Odia workers outside the state) / 0674-3120552 (OB&OCWW Board office, Bhubaneswar)
